title: Casemiro says Michael Carrick ‘completely deserves’ Manchester United appointment
content:
Casemiro has joined Manchester United team-mates Kobbie Mainoo and Matheus Cunha in calling for Michael Carrick to remain as the club’s head coach beyond this season.

Casemiro, who will leave Old Trafford when his contract expires at the end of the season, said Carrick “completely deserves” the job after guiding the club back into the Champions League with a sharp upturn in form.

The 44-year-old was appointed United head coach on a deal for the remainder of the campaign, succeeding Ruben Amorim, with the club seventh in the Premier League.

Carrick has collected 32 points from 14 games in charge, more than any other team in the league in that period, to see United rise to third in the table — six points clear of Liverpool in fourth and 12 ahead of sixth-place Bournemouth, meaning Champions League qualification has been secured with three games remaining.

“Of course he deserves it, and he deserves the club’s total trust,” Casemiro, 34, told ESPN Brasil of Carrick.

“He has been doing an incredible job and I think that with more time he has everything to be a great manager of Manchester United.”

Casemiro added: “He managed to change the club and me in particular, even more so because he was a former player, a midfielder.

“I’m happy for the person he is, the guy is a sensational person, an incredible person, and he deserves everything that’s happening in his career.”

After Sunday’s win over Liverpool, United’s match-winner Mainoo said of Carrick: “He gives so much confidence to not just me but all the players. You want to follow him, you want to fight for him, you want to die for him on the pitch.”

Cunha, Casemiro’s team-mate at club and international level for Brazil, said Carrick “has the magic” of the era of Sir Alex Ferguson, who won 13 Premier League titles at Old Trafford.

“How he teaches everyone is amazing,” Cunha said of Carrick. “It’s amazing. He’s a pleasure. Of course, I think he deserves it.”

Casemiro added he would leave United this summer “through the front door” and described his four years at the club, where he won the Carabao Cup and FA Cup, had been a “beautiful time” in his career.
